question: After the companion execution-commit defect is repaired, should exec denylist policy remain supported in both openclaw.json and exec-approvals.json, or have one canonical persisted owner?
rationale: This choice determines compatibility, hot-reload behavior, remote-node visibility, protocol persistence, and which component owns final authorization.

options.title: Single approval-policy owner
options.body: Keep denylist in exec-approvals.json and remove the parallel openclaw.json surface to minimize split authority and upgrade complexity.

options.title: Dual persisted surfaces
options.body: Accept both surfaces and permanently own their union, hot-reload, remote-host, and upgrade semantics.

recommendation.title: Single approval-policy owner
recommendation.body: Keep denylist in exec-approvals.json and remove the parallel openclaw.json surface to minimize split authority and upgrade complexity.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent merged macOS approval hardening establishes the final authorization boundary affected by this decision.
